readings: Using the town or city of the customer who placed the order behind each invoice line item: first, for each order item id and town, average the line `product_price` and the ratio `derived_product_cost` / `derived_total_cost`, ignoring missing values; then average those per town. Which towns have an average cost ratio above the average across all towns? Show the town, its average price, its average ratio, and how far its ratio is above the cross-town average, without rounding.
queries:
WITH item_averages AS (
    SELECT
        il.order_item_id,
        c.town_city,
        AVG(il.product_price) AS average_price,
        AVG(il.derived_product_cost / il.derived_total_cost) AS average_ratio
    FROM Invoice_Line_Items AS il
    JOIN Invoices AS i ON i.invoice_number = il.invoice_number
    JOIN Orders AS o ON o.order_id = i.order_id
    JOIN Customers AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
    GROUP BY il.order_item_id, c.town_city
),
town_averages AS (
    SELECT
        town_city,
        AVG(average_price) AS average_price,
        AVG(average_ratio) AS average_ratio
    FROM item_averages
    GROUP BY town_city
),
cross_town_average AS (
    SELECT AVG(average_ratio) AS average_ratio
    FROM town_averages
)
SELECT
    t.town_city,
    t.average_price,
    t.average_ratio,
    t.average_ratio - x.average_ratio AS ratio_above_average
FROM town_averages AS t
CROSS JOIN cross_town_average AS x
WHERE t.average_ratio > x.average_ratio
